newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen slip on profit-taking,Nikkei rebound.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen slip on profit-taking,Nikkei rebound.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures came under pressure from profit-taking and the Tokyo stock market's sharp, unexpected rebound on Monday after a series of declines last week.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.31 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.35. Turnover was low at 5,189 lots.

The 225-share Nikkei average surged 815.14 points or 4.71 percent to end at 18,118.79 after losing more than 2,000 points last week on worries about the economy and the health of financial institutions.
Dealers said Monday's rebound was largely driven by technical factors and could prove short-lived as sentiment on the Japanese stock market remained poor.

Japanese government bond futures for March settled at 125.66 against their opening 125.40. Dealers said the contract looked very toppish as reflected by its slow gains despite the Nikkei's near 1,000-point drop on Friday.
"The trading range is already very high so everybody is a bit cautious," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
He said investors were likely to cash in their gains and square their positions ahead of the Japanese financial year end on March 31, 1997.

Eurodollar futures had a sluggish session with interest hamstrung by fears of a U.S. interest rate hike after the release of a stronger than expected December non-farm payrolls report on Friday. "The fear of inflation is coming back again so the selling pressure has gradually increased. People are talking about a rate hike in February or March," said the trader.
